subject: math
title: Grade 8 Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
seo_title: Grade 8 Multiplying and Dividing Fractions Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Operations with fractions (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and order of operations)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on multiplying and dividing fractions, matched to the BC curriculum: area models, simplifying first, mixed numbers, dividing by the reciprocal, order of operations (BEDMAS) and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators and the denominators. To divide, flip only the fraction you divide by and multiply.
key_sub: 3/4 ÷ 3/8 = 3/4 × 8/3 = 2, not 4/3 × 3/8. Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first, and follow BEDMAS: × and ÷ before + and −.
body_html:
The big idea

× a fraction means “of”. 23 × 34 means 23 of 34. ÷ a fraction asks “how many fit?” 56 ÷ 13 asks how many thirds fit in 56.

Multiply fractions

Multiply the numerators. Multiply the denominators. Then simplify. The area model shows why: the square is cut into 3 × 4 = 12 small rectangles.

Example 1

58 × 415 = ?

Simplify first. 5 and 15 share 5: they become 1 and 3. 4 and 8 share 4: they become 1 and 2. Now 12 × 13 = 16.

Answer: 16

Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first.

Example 2

2 12 × 1 15 = ?

Write 2 12 as 52 and 1 15 as 65. 52 × 65 = 3010 = 3.

Answer: 3

Divide fractions

Count how many groups fit, or use the rule: keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction (use its reciprocal). Flip only the number you divide by.

Example 3

3 34 ÷ 56 = ?

Write 3 34 as 154. Keep 154, flip 56 to 65: 154 × 65 = 9020 = 4 12. Check: 4 12 × 56 = 92 × 56 = 4512 = 3 34.

Answer: 4 12

Order of operations (BEDMAS)

Fractions follow the same order as whole numbers: brackets, exponents, then × and ÷ from left to right, then + and − from left to right.

Example 4

13 + 12 × 45 = ?

Multiply first: 12 × 45 = 25. Then 13 + 25 = 515 + 615 = 1115.

Answer: 1115

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
34 ÷ 38 = 43 × 38 (flipping the wrong fraction)Keep the first fraction. Flip only the divisor: 34 × 83 = 2.
23 × 45 = 68 (adding across)Multiply across: 2 × 43 × 5 = 815.
2 12 × 3 13 = 6 16 (multiplying the whole parts and the fraction parts separately)Change to improper fractions first: 52 × 103 = 253 = 8 13.
13 + 12 × 45 = 56 × 45 (adding first)Multiply before you add: the answer is 1115.

faq.q: How do you multiply fractions and mixed numbers in Grade 8?
faq.a: Change any mixed numbers to improper fractions, multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, then simplify. For example, 2 1/2 × 1 1/5 = 5/2 × 6/5 = 30/10 = 3.

faq.q: When you divide fractions, which fraction do you flip?
faq.a: Flip only the second fraction, the one you divide by. Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and multiply by the reciprocal: 3/4 ÷ 3/8 = 3/4 × 8/3 = 2.
Yes. Do brackets, then exponents, then × and ÷ from left to right, then + and − from left to right. For example, 1/3 + 1/2 × 4/5 = 1/3 + 2/5 = 11/15.

faq.q: When do BC students learn to multiply and divide fractions?
faq.a: In Grade 8. The BC Grade 8 math curriculum lists operations with fractions, including multiplication, division and order of operations, under Computational fluency. In Grade 9 these operations are extended to rational numbers, including negative fractions.

items.q: The model shows 23 × 35. What fraction of the whole square is dark? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 5 × 3 = 15 equal small rectangles, and 3 × 2 = 6 of them are dark. So 23 × 35 = 615 = 25.

items.q: The model shows 12 × 34. What fraction of the whole square is dark? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 4 × 2 = 8 equal small rectangles, and 3 × 1 = 3 of them are dark. So 12 × 34 = 38.

items.q: The model shows 34 × 45. What fraction of the whole square is dark? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 5 × 4 = 20 equal small rectangles, and 4 × 3 = 12 of them are dark. So 34 × 45 = 1220 = 35.

items.q: The square is 1 whole. The light columns are 34 of the square, and the dark part is a part of the light columns. Which multiplication does the dark part show?
c: 23 + 34
13 × 34
23 × 14
23 × 34
items.e: The light part is 3 of 4 columns: 34 of the square. The dark part is 2 of the 3 rows of the light part. So the dark part is 23 of 34: 23 × 34 = 612 = 12.

items.q: 13 × 25 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 13 × 25 = 1 × 23 × 5 = 215.

items.q: 34 × 35 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 34 × 35 = 3 × 34 × 5 = 920.

items.q: 27 × 34 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 27 × 34 = 2 × 37 × 4 = 628 = 314.

items.q: 58 × 13 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 58 × 13 = 5 × 18 × 3 = 524.

items.q: 45 × 23 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 45 × 23 = 4 × 25 × 3 = 815.

items.q: 16 × 37 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 16 × 37 = 1 × 36 × 7 = 342 = 114.

items.q: 29 × 45 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 29 × 45 = 2 × 49 × 5 = 845.

items.q: 38 × 38 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 38 × 38 = 3 × 38 × 8 = 964.

items.q: 58 × 415 = ?
items.e: Simplify first: divide 5 and 15 by 5, and divide 4 and 8 by 4. Now 12 × 13 = 16.

items.q: 914 × 712 = ?
items.e: Simplify first: divide 9 and 12 by 3, and divide 7 and 14 by 7. Now 32 × 14 = 38.

items.q: 625 × 109 = ?
items.e: Simplify first: divide 6 and 9 by 3, and divide 10 and 25 by 5. Now 25 × 23 = 415.

items.q: 821 × 149 = ?
items.e: Simplify first: divide 14 and 21 by 7. Now 83 × 29 = 1627.

items.q: Wei wants to simplify 635 × 149 before multiplying, so he divides 6 and 14 by 2. What is wrong?
c: Nothing. Any two numbers that share a factor can be divided.
6 and 14 are both numerators. Pair a numerator with a denominator.
You can never simplify before multiplying.
items.e: Dividing two numerators changes the value. Pair each numerator with a denominator: 6 and 9 share 3, and 14 and 35 share 7. Then 25 × 23 = 415. 6 and 14 are both numerators, so he cannot divide them both.

items.q: 6 × 23 = ?
items.e: Write 6 as 61. 61 × 23 = 123 = 4. Multiply only the numerator by 6. (1218 is wrong: it multiplies the denominator too.)

items.q:
10 × 34 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 10 as 101. 101 × 34 = 304 = 152 = 7 12. Check: 34 of 10 is a bit less than 10.

items.q: Without calculating, which product is greater than 35?
c: 35 × 45
35 × 54
35 × 12
items.e: Multiplying by a number greater than 1 makes the answer greater. 54 is greater than 1, so 35 × 54 is greater than 35. 35 × 1 = 35, and 45 and 12 are less than 1.

items.q: Write 2 34 as an improper fraction.
items.e: 2 wholes are 2 × 4 = 8 fourths. Add the 3 fourths: 8 + 3 = 11. So 2 34 = 114.

items.q: Write 3 25 as an improper fraction.
items.e: 3 wholes are 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Add the 2 fifths: 15 + 2 = 17. So 3 25 = 175.

items.q: 2 12 × 25 = ?
items.e: Write 2 12 as 52. Simplify first: the 5s cancel, and the 2s cancel. Now 1 × 1 = 1.

items.q:
2 13 × 34 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 2 13 as 73. Simplify first: the 3s cancel. Now 7 × 14 = 74 = 1 34.

items.q:
2 14 × 23 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 2 14 as 94. Simplify first: divide 9 and 3 by 3, and divide 2 and 4 by 2. Now 32 × 1 = 32 = 1 12.

items.q: 2 34 × 811 = ?
items.e: Write 2 34 as 114. Simplify first: the 11s cancel, and divide 8 and 4 by 4. Now 1 × 2 = 2.

items.q:
1 12 × 1 23 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 1 12 as 32. Write 1 23 as 53. Simplify first: the 3s cancel. Now 12 × 5 = 52 = 2 12.

items.q:
1 34 × 1 15 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 1 34 as 74. Write 1 15 as 65. Simplify first: divide 6 and 4 by 2. Now 72 × 35 = 2110 = 2 110.

items.q: 3 13 × 1 45 = ?
items.e: Write 3 13 as 103. Write 1 45 as 95. Simplify first: divide 10 and 5 by 5, and divide 9 and 3 by 3. Now 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q:
1 14 × 2 13 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 1 14 as 54. Write 2 13 as 73. 54 × 73 = 5 × 74 × 3 = 3512 = 2 1112.

items.q: 2 23 × 3 34 = ?
items.e: Write 2 23 as 83. Write 3 34 as 154. Simplify first: divide 8 and 4 by 4, and divide 15 and 3 by 3. Now 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q:
2 35 × 56 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 2 35 as 135. Simplify first: the 5s cancel. Now 13 × 16 = 136 = 2 16.

items.q:
4 12 × 1 16 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 4 12 as 92. Write 1 16 as 76. Simplify first: divide 9 and 6 by 3. Now 32 × 72 = 214 = 5 14.

items.q:
1 56 × 2 14 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 1 56 as 116. Write 2 14 as 94. Simplify first: divide 9 and 6 by 3. Now 112 × 34 = 338 = 4 18.

items.q:
3 × 2 14 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 2 14 as 94. 3 × 94 = 274 = 6 34. (6 14 multiplies only the 2 by 3, not the 14.)

items.q:
4 × 1 23 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 1 23 as 53. 4 × 53 = 203 = 6 23. Check: 4 × 1 = 4 and 4 × 23 = 83 = 2 23, and 4 + 2 23 = 6 23.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 3 78 × 2 19?
items.e: Round each mixed number to the nearest whole number: 3 78 is close to 4 and 2 19 is close to 2. 4 × 2 = 8, so the product is about 8. (3 × 2 = 6 ignores the 78.)

items.q: Hana says 2 12 × 3 13 = 6 16, because 2 × 3 = 6 and 12 × 13 = 16. What is wrong?
c: She should have flipped 3 13.
She forgot to simplify 16.
She multiplied the whole parts and the fraction parts separately.
items.e: A mixed number is a sum, so its parts cannot be multiplied separately. Change to improper fractions: 52 × 103 = 506 = 253 = 8 13. Hana multiplied the whole parts and the fraction parts separately.

items.q: 1 12 × ? = 2
items.e: Divide: 2 ÷ 1 12 = 2 ÷ 32 = 2 × 23 = 43 = 1 13. Check: 32 × 43 = 126 = 2.

items.q: Without calculating, which product is greater than 2 12?
c: 2 12 × 12
2 12 × 45
2 12 × 1 15
items.e: Multiplying by a number greater than 1 makes the answer greater. 1 15 is greater than 1, so 2 12 × 1 15 is greater than 2 12. (It equals 52 × 65 = 3.)

sets.title: Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 47?
items.e: Flip the fraction: the reciprocal of 47 is 74. Check: 47 × 74 = 2828 = 1. (−47 is the opposite, not the reciprocal.)

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 2 13?
items.e: First write 2 13 as an improper fraction: 73. Then flip it: 37. Check: 73 × 37 = 1. Do not flip only the 13.

items.q: The bar shows 34. How many groups of 38 fit in 34? 34 ÷ 38 = ?
items.e: Use eighths: 34 = 68. Each group is 3 eighths. 6 eighths make 6 ÷ 3 = 2 groups. So 34 ÷ 38 = 2. Check: 2 × 38 = 34.

items.q: The bar shows 23. How many groups of 14 fit in 23? 23 ÷ 14 = ?
items.e: Use twelfths: 23 = 812 and 14 = 312. Each group is 3 twelfths. 8 twelfths make 2 full groups, with 2 twelfths left over. Those 2 twelfths are 23 of a group. So 23 ÷ 14 = 2 23. Check: 2 23 × 14 = 23.

items.q: The bar shows 1 14. How many groups of 12 fit in 1 14? 1 14 ÷ 12 = ?
items.e: Use fourths: 1 14 = 54 and 12 = 24. Each group is 2 fourths. 5 fourths make 2 full groups, with 1 fourth left over. That 1 fourth is 12 of a group. So 1 14 ÷ 12 = 2 12. Check: 2 12 × 12 = 1 14.

items.q: Which multiplication has the same answer as 35 ÷ 27?
c: 53 × 72
35 × 27
53 × 27
35 × 72
items.e: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second fraction, the one you divide by: 35 × 72. Do not flip 35.

items.q: Which multiplication has the same answer as 49 ÷ 56?
c: 94 × 56
49 × 65
94 × 65
49 × 56
items.e: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second fraction, the one you divide by: 49 × 65. Do not flip 49.

items.q: 23 ÷ 16 = ?
items.e: Keep 23, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 16 to 6. Simplify first: divide 6 and 3 by 3. Now 2 × 2 = 4. Check: 4 × 16 = 23.

items.q: 35 ÷ 910 = ?
items.e: Keep 35, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 910 to 109. Simplify first: divide 3 and 9 by 3, and divide 10 and 5 by 5. Now 1 × 23 = 23. Check: 23 × 910 = 35.

items.q: 58 ÷ 34 = ?
items.e: Keep 58, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 34 to 43. Simplify first: divide 4 and 8 by 4. Now 52 × 13 = 56. Check: 56 × 34 = 58.

items.q:
710 ÷ 25 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Keep 710, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 25 to 52. Simplify first: divide 5 and 10 by 5. Now 72 × 12 = 74 = 1 34. Check: 1 34 × 25 = 710.

items.q:
89 ÷ 415 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Keep 89, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 415 to 154. Simplify first: divide 8 and 4 by 4, and divide 15 and 9 by 3. Now 23 × 5 = 103 = 3 13. Check: 3 13 × 415 = 89.

items.q: 37 ÷ 67 = ?
items.e: Keep 37, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 67 to 76. Simplify first: divide 3 and 6 by 3, and the 7s cancel. Now 1 × 12 = 12. Check: 12 × 67 = 37.

items.q:
56 ÷ 59 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Keep 56, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 59 to 95. Simplify first: the 5s cancel, and divide 9 and 6 by 3. Now 12 × 3 = 32 = 1 12. Check: 1 12 × 59 = 56.

items.q:
3 34 ÷ 56 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 3 34 as 154. Keep 154, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 56 to 65. Simplify first: divide 15 and 5 by 5, and divide 6 and 4 by 2. Now 32 × 3 = 92 = 4 12. Check: 4 12 × 56 = 3 34.

items.q:
3 13 ÷ 1 14 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 3 13 as 103. Write 1 14 as 54. Keep 103, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 54 to 45. Simplify first: divide 10 and 5 by 5. Now 23 × 4 = 83 = 2 23. Check: 2 23 × 1 14 = 3 13.

items.q: 4 12 ÷ 1 12 = ?
items.e: Write 4 12 as 92. Write 1 12 as 32. Keep 92, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 32 to 23. Simplify first: divide 9 and 3 by 3, and the 2s cancel. Now 3 × 1 = 3. Check: 3 × 1 12 = 4 12.

items.q:
3 15 ÷ 2 23 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Write 3 15 as 165. Write 2 23 as 83. Keep 165, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 83 to 38. Simplify first: divide 16 and 8 by 8. Now 25 × 3 = 65 = 1 15. Check: 1 15 × 2 23 = 3 15.

items.q: 6 ÷ 34 = ?
items.e: Keep 6, change ÷ to ×, and flip 34 to 43. 6 × 43 = 243 = 8. Check: 8 × 34 = 244 = 6. (34 ÷ 6 = 18 flips the wrong number.)

items.q: Emma writes 34 ÷ 38 = 43 × 38 = 12. What mistake did she make?
c: She flipped 34 instead of 38.
items.e: Emma flipped the first fraction. Flip only the divisor: 34 × 83 = 2412 = 2. Check: 2 × 38 = 68 = 34. So she flipped 34 instead of 38.

items.q: 13 + 12 × 45 = ?
items.e: Multiply first: 12 × 45 = 410 = 25. Then 13 + 25 = 515 + 615 = 1115.

items.q: 34 − 12 ÷ 3 = ?
items.e: Divide first: 12 ÷ 3 = 12 × 13 = 16. Then 34 − 16 = 912 − 212 = 712.

items.q: (56 − 13) × 49 = ?
items.e: Brackets first: 56 − 13 = 56 − 26 = 36 = 12. Then 12 × 49 = 418 = 29.

items.q: 23 ÷ 49 × 12 = ?
items.e: ÷ and × have the same rank, so work from left to right. 23 ÷ 49 = 23 × 94 = 1812 = 32. Then 32 × 12 = 34.

items.q: (23)² + 19 = ?
items.e: Exponent first: (23)² = 23 × 23 = 49. Then 49 + 19 = 59. (Squaring is not × 2.)

items.q: 3 − 1 12 × 43 = ?
items.e: Multiply first: 1 12 × 43 = 32 × 43 = 126 = 2. Then 3 − 2 = 1.

items.q:
1 34 × (12 + 13) = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Brackets first: 12 + 13 = 36 + 26 = 56. Then 1 34 × 56 = 74 × 56 = 3524 = 1 1124.

items.q:
56 ÷ (14 + 13) = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Brackets first: 14 + 13 = 312 + 412 = 712. Then 56 ÷ 712 = 56 × 127 = 107 = 1 37.

items.q: (35)² ÷ 910 = ?
items.e: Exponent first: (35)² = 925. Then 925 ÷ 910 = 925 × 109 = 1025 = 25.

items.q:
78 − 14 + 12 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: + and − have the same rank, so work from left to right. 78 − 14 = 78 − 28 = 58. Then 58 + 12 = 58 + 48 = 98 = 1 18.

items.q:
4 12 − 2 14 × 1 13 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Multiply first: 2 14 × 1 13 = 94 × 43. The 4s cancel, and 9 and 3 share 3, so the product is 3. Then 4 12 − 3 = 1 12.

items.q:
23 × 38 + 34 ÷ 12 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Multiply and divide first: 23 × 38 = 624 = 14, and 34 ÷ 12 = 34 × 2 = 64. Then 14 + 64 = 74 = 1 34.

items.q: (1 − 38) × (1 + 15) = ?
items.e: Brackets first: 1 − 38 = 58 and 1 + 15 = 65. Then 58 × 65 = 3040 = 34.

items.q: 23 ÷ (12 − 16) = ?
items.e: Brackets first: 12 − 16 = 36 − 16 = 26 = 13. Then 23 ÷ 13 = 23 × 3 = 2.

items.q: 59 ÷ 56 − 13 = ?
items.e: Divide first: 59 ÷ 56 = 59 × 65. The 5s cancel: 69 = 23. Then 23 − 13 = 13.

items.q: 12 + 25 ÷ 45 = ?
items.e: Divide first: 25 ÷ 45 = 25 × 54 = 1020 = 12. Then 12 + 12 = 1.

items.q:
2 12 ÷ 56 − 1 13 = ?
Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide first: 2 12 ÷ 56 = 52 × 65 = 3010 = 3. Then 3 − 1 13 = 1 23.

items.q: Evaluate 4a − b when a = 56 and b = 23.
items.e: 4a means 4 × a: 4 × 56 = 206 = 103. Then 103 − 23 = 83 = 2 23. (4a is not 4 56.)

items.q: Evaluate x² + x when x = 34.
items.e: x² = (34)² = 916. Then 916 + 34 = 916 + 1216 = 2116 = 1 516. (x² means x × x, not 2 × x.)

items.q: Kai says 34 − 14 × 2 = 1. What did he do wrong?
items.e: (34 − 14) × 2 = 12 × 2 = 1, so Kai subtracted first. BEDMAS says multiply first: 14 × 2 = 12, then 34 − 12 = 14. He subtracted before multiplying.

sets.title: Word problems: recipes, trails and BC trips

items.q: A pan of Nanaimo bars needs 34 cup of butter. Ryan makes 12 of the recipe. How much butter does he need?
items.e: 12 of 34 means 12 × 34. 12 × 34 = 1 × 32 × 4 = 38 cup.

items.q: One batch of pancakes needs 23 cup of milk. Jasleen makes 2 12 batches for a ski trip breakfast. How much milk does she need?
items.e: 2 12 batches of 23 cup: multiply. Write 2 12 as 52. Simplify first: the 2s cancel. Now 5 × 13 = 53 = 1 23 cups.

items.q: Liam’s walk along the Stanley Park seawall is 4 12 km long. He has walked 23 of it. How far has he walked?
items.e: 23 of 4 12 km means 23 × 4 12. Write 4 12 as 92. Simplify first: the 2s cancel, and divide 9 and 3 by 3. Now 1 × 3 = 3 km.

items.q: On a trail near Squamish, Owen hikes 3 34 km in 1 14 h. At this rate, how far does he hike in 1 h?
items.e: Divide the distance by the time. Write 3 34 as 154. Write 1 14 as 54. Keep 154, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 54 to 45. Simplify first: divide 15 and 5 by 5, and the 4s cancel. Now 3 × 1 = 3 km. Check: 3 × 1 14 = 3 34.

items.q: Mei has 2 14 m of fabric to make banners for the school’s Terry Fox Run. Each banner needs 34 m. How many banners can she make?
items.e: How many 34 m pieces fit in 2 14 m? Divide. Write 2 14 as 94. Keep 94, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 34 to 43. Simplify first: divide 9 and 3 by 3, and the 4s cancel. Now 3 × 1 = 3 banners. Check: 3 × 34 = 2 14.

items.q: A family buys 1 12 kg of fresh salmon in Steveston. They cut it into portions of 316 kg. How many portions do they get?
items.e: How many 316 kg portions fit in 1 12 kg? Divide. Write 1 12 as 32. Keep 32, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 316 to 163. Simplify first: the 3s cancel, and divide 16 and 2 by 2. Now 1 × 8 = 8 portions. Check: 8 × 316 = 1 12.

items.q: Noah is building a planter box. A cedar board is 2 23 m long, and he cuts it into pieces that are each 23 m long. How many pieces does he get?
items.e: How many 23 m pieces fit in 2 23 m? Divide. Write 2 23 as 83. Keep 83, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 23 to 32. Simplify first: divide 8 and 2 by 2, and the 3s cancel. Now 4 × 1 = 4 pieces. Check: 4 × 23 = 2 23.

items.q: A rectangular garden bed is 2 12 m long and 1 35 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width. Write 2 12 as 52. Write 1 35 as 85. Simplify first: the 5s cancel, and divide 8 and 2 by 2. Now 1 × 4 = 4 m².

items.q: A BC Ferries trip from Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay takes about 1 12 h. Olivia reads for 23 of the trip. For how long does she read?
items.e: 23 of 1 12 h means 23 × 1 12. Write 1 12 as 32. Simplify first: the 2s cancel, and the 3s cancel. Now 1 × 1 = 1 h.

items.q: A jug holds 1 34 L of apple juice from the Okanagan. Each cup holds 14 L. How many cups can be filled?
items.e: How many 14 L cups fit in 1 34 L? Divide. Write 1 34 as 74. Keep 74, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 14 to 4. Simplify first: the 4s cancel. Now 7 × 1 = 7 cups. Check: 7 × 14 = 1 34.

items.q: Ava uses 23 of a can of stain to stain 45 of a fence. How much stain does she need for the whole fence?
c: 56 of a can
815 of a can
items.e: Stain for the whole fence = stain used ÷ fraction of the fence stained. Keep 23, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 45 to 54. Simplify first: divide 2 and 4 by 2. Now 13 × 52 = 56 of a can. Check: 56 × 45 = 23.

items.q: 35 of the Grade 8 students go on a field trip to Victoria. 23 of those students visit the Royal BC Museum. What fraction of the Grade 8 students visit the museum?
c: 25 of the students
1 415 of the students
58 of the students
1 19 of the students
items.e: 23 of 35 means 23 × 35. Simplify first: the 3s cancel. Now 2 × 15 = 25 of the students.

items.q: In Vancouver, 4 12 cm of rain fell over 6 days, the same amount each day. How much rain fell each day?
items.e: Share 4 12 cm equally over 6 days: 4 12 ÷ 6. Write 4 12 as 92 and flip 6 to 16. 92 × 16 = 912 = 34 cm. Check: 6 × 34 = 184 = 4 12.

items.q: Ethan has 3 12 cups of flour. One batch of oatmeal cookies needs 34 cup. How many full batches can he make?
items.e: Write 3 12 as 72. Keep 72, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 34 to 43. Simplify first: divide 4 and 2 by 2. Now 7 × 23 = 143 = 4 23. Check: 4 23 × 34 = 3 12. Only full batches count, so he can make 4 batches.

items.q: A rope is 4 12 m long. It is cut into pieces that are each 38 m long. Which expression gives the number of pieces?
c: 38 ÷ 4 12
4 12 ÷ 38
4 12 × 38
4 12 − 38
items.e: The question asks how many 38 m pieces fit in 4 12 m, so divide by 38: 4 12 ÷ 38 = 92 × 83 = 12 pieces.

items.q: Simran has paddled a canoe 2 14 km. That is 34 of the route around a lake. How long is the whole route?
items.e: 34 of the route is 2 14 km, so the whole route is 2 14 ÷ 34. Write 2 14 as 94. Keep 94, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 34 to 43. Simplify first: divide 9 and 3 by 3, and the 4s cancel. Now 3 × 1 = 3 km. Check: 3 × 34 = 2 14.

items.q: Sofia has 5 m of rope. She cuts 3 pieces that are each 1 14 m long. How much rope is left?
items.e: Rope left = 5 − 3 × 1 14. Multiply first: 3 × 1 14 = 3 × 54 = 154 = 3 34 m. Then 5 − 3 34 = 1 14 m.

items.q: A recipe for 24 muffins uses 2 14 cups of flour. Arjun wants to make 16 muffins. How much flour does he need?
items.e: 16 muffins is 1624 = 23 of the recipe. 23 × 2 14 = 23 × 94. The 3s cancel, and 2 and 4 share 2: 32 = 1 12 cups.

items.q: A school orders 12 pizzas for a Grade 8 year-end party. Each student eats 38 of a pizza. How many students can be served?
items.e: How many 38 fit in 12? Divide: 12 ÷ 38 = 12 × 83 = 963 = 32 students. Check: 32 × 38 = 968 = 12.

items.q: Chloe spends 25 of her savings on a skateboard. Then she spends 12 of the rest on a helmet. What fraction of her savings does she spend on the helmet?
c: 15 of the savings
910 of the savings
310 of the savings
12 of the savings
items.e: The rest is 1 − 25 = 35 of the savings. 12 of 35 is 12 × 35 = 310 of the savings.
